references.text: Elisha raises the Shunammite's son from the dead by lying over the child and calling him to life, which parallels Jesus taking the girl by the hand and commanding her to rise.
Mark's parallel account of the raising of Jairus' daughter, where Jesus takes the child by the hand and says "Talita kumi" – "Little girl, get up!"
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus takes the girl by the hand and she gets up.
Peter raises Tabitha from the dead with the words "Tabitha, get up!", which reflects Jesus' command to Jairus' daughter.
Jesus raises the widow's son at Nain by speaking to the dead and commanding him to rise, a parallel to his command for the dead girl to rise.
Jesus calls out to the dead Lazarus and commands him to come out of the tomb, demonstrating the same divine authority over death as when he commanded Jairus' daughter to rise.
Elijah stretches himself over the widow's dead son and cries out to the Lord, and the boy is brought back to life – an Old Testament foreshadowing of Jesus raising the dead girl.
